1.explanation:
1. headless-chrome.md — shows how to launch Chrome with extensions enabled (`--enable-extensions`) and the remote debugging port for reproducing via `yarn chrome`.
2. puppeteer.md — explains how the CLI (`cli/index.js`) uses Puppeteer under the hood to drive Lighthouse and how to pass flags like `--port=9222` and `--view`.
3. configuration.md — details how Lighthouse configurations and flags are set, which is needed to reproduce different audit runs (DevTools vs. CLI).
4. new-audits.md — describes how audits are structured in Lighthouse, including how they gather data (and what execution contexts they inspect), so you can understand why the no-unload-listeners audit misses isolated-context listeners.
5. understanding-results.md — walks through how audit results render in the report UI (tables, failure reasons, links) to correlate the Markdown output with the screenshots.
6. hacking-tips.md — provides guidance on debugging Lighthouse itself (e.g. cycling execution contexts in DevTools, using `getEventListeners` in different contexts), which is crucial to diagnose this isolated-context listener issue.
1.bug_scenario:
When Lighthouse runs its back/forward cache (bfcache) audit on a page with the LastPass extension loaded, the audit reports a failure “The page has an unload handler in the main frame” (image 1). Yet immediately after, the separate “Avoids unload event listeners” audit shows a green pass and lists no unload listeners at all (image 2). In other words, the bfcache audit detects an unload listener injected by the extension’s content script, but the no-unload-listeners audit—and even manual calls to getEventListeners(window) in DevTools—see nothing. This mismatch stems from that listener living in an isolated execution context the audit doesn’t inspect.

Key UI elements:
- The red bfcache audit banner and its “Failure reason” table row
- The message text describing “unload handler in the main frame”
- The green “Avoids unload event listeners” audit banner with no listeners listed
- The link targets (“Learn more about the bfcache” / “unload event listeners”)
